body:
As I walked past the building, my eyes fell on a small mailbox overflowing with letters in different languages. The name written on one envelope was almost illegible — perhaps even a mix-up between names. But as I bent down to read it, my fingers brushing against a familiar handwriting, a wave of recognition washed over me. It was the last address before the old street ended, just as it had been when I delivered the final package. My heart pounded but I took a deep breath, feeling a surge of mixed emotions.

The door creaked open slowly, revealing a figure standing there, their back turned away from me. My mind raced. Should I call out? Was this someone from the landlord’s list?

No, I decided firmly. There were far more important things to attend to than this moment of anger or confusion. With a steadier hand, I reached into my pocket for some paper to write a letter or an apology note later.
